flagged.evidence: The item says the bilateral integral is the symmetric-truncation limit and cites [[def-improper-integral-at-infinity]]. That dependency defines only the one-sided integrals over [a,∞) and (−∞,b]; it does not supply the cited bilateral convention.

The current item defines G_n as an “absolutely convergent improper multiple integral,” then applies Fubini to factor it. The cited Fubini theorem assumes a product-measurable function in L¹(μ×ν) and equates Lebesgue product and iterated integrals. The item does not define its n-dimensional improper-integral convention or identify that integral with the Lebesgue product integral, so the application does not establish the claimed factorization for G_n as defined.

The Hermite recurrence dependency states g_n=H_n g_0/√(2ⁿn!) with H_n a polynomial. But step 1.2 starts by assuming ⟨f,g_n⟩=0 and derives vanishing moments; step 3.1 then says this proves the moment criterion (a), whose hypothesis is vanishing moments. The missing reverse implication is immediate from the recurrence formula and the completeness established by the argument, so this is nonfatal.
